blocks.text: Jacobsen Townhomes South Surrey: streets and boundaries

items.t: Jacobsen is a single townhome development addressed as 2687 158 Street in Grandview Heights, South Surrey, assembled in part from 2660 Croydon Drive.

blocks.text: Jacobsen Townhomes South Surrey: the housing stock

items.t: Jacobsen was permitted as 65 townhouse units, per the City's March 12, 2012 planning report for the site.
The 2012 proposal required an Official Community Plan (OCP) amendment from Suburban to Multiple Residential, plus rezoning and a development permit, before the townhouses could proceed.

blocks.text: Jacobsen Townhomes South Surrey: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Jacobsen's zone change was from A-2 and RA (Acreage Residential) to RM-30, the townhouse residential zone the project was built under — not a site-specific Comprehensive Development zone like Greenway's.

A development variance permit formed part of the 2012 approval package, so the built form includes varied items — confirm any alteration against the permit and the strata bylaws, not the standard RM-30 text alone.

blocks.text: Jacobsen Townhomes South Surrey: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Jacobsen's approval predates Greenway's by four years (2012 against 2016), so its building systems and depreciation-report items sit on an earlier cycle than its neighbour's.

Morgan Crossing and Grandview Corners, at 160 Street and 24 Avenue, are the commercial core the Grandview plans were built around — Jacobsen's daily shopping runs north to that corner, not into White Rock.

blocks.text: Jacobsen Townhomes South Surrey: getting around

items.t: Highway 99 access is via the 24 Avenue and 32 Avenue interchanges west of the development.

blocks.text: Jacobsen Townhomes South Surrey: risks and due diligence

items.t: Start with the depreciation report — a 2012-approved wood-frame townhouse complex is now into the window where roof, deck and envelope items dominate the 30-year projection.
Check the Form B for approved-but-unpaid special levies, the contingency reserve fund balance and the water-damage deductible in the insurance summary.

blocks.text: Inside Grandview Heights, Jacobsen offers a townhome option. It’s a good first step into a townhome, especially for families who want the Sunnyside and Grandview Heights Secondary catchments.

faq.a: The March 12, 2012 planning report for 2687 158 Street and part of 2660 Croydon Drive lists Croydon Ventures Inc. and Norma Jean Svab as owners, with the project proceeding as a 65-unit townhouse rezoning — so a buyer who wants a builder name should ask for it in the disclosure and strata records rather than rely on marketing material.

faq.q: How is Jacobsen different from Greenway, one street over?
faq.a: The approvals are different in kind. Jacobsen was rezoned to the standard RM-30 townhouse zone at a plan density of 20 to 30 units per acre for 65 homes, while Greenway was rezoned to a site-specific CD zone at 15 to 25 units per acre for 67 homes — the two complexes follow different bylaws even though they share the Grandview bench.

faq.q: Was Jacobsen always planned as townhouses?
faq.a: No — the land started as suburban acreage. The 2012 application had to amend the OCP designation from Suburban to Multiple Residential and rezone from A-2 and RA before any townhouse could be built, which is why the complex sits among later Grandview subdivisions rather than in an older townhouse cluster.

Grandview Heights Secondary at 16987 25 Avenue serves the wider Grandview Heights area; the elementary catchment for this specific Croydon Drive edge address must be confirmed for the unit being bought, not assumed from the neighbourhood name.
